explainer.lead: The transformer is the attention-based architecture introduced in “Attention Is All You Need,” dispensing with recurrence to become the foundation of modern LLMs. Its parallelizable design made training on large datasets practical.

tiers.eli5: Instead of reading a sentence one word at a time, the model looks at all the words at once and works out which ones matter to each other.
tiers.practitioner: Tokenize input, embed tokens, then contextualize them across the context window with parallel multi-head attention at each layer. The pitfall: self-attention alone is permutation-invariant, so positional information must be injected or token order is lost.
tiers.paperLevel: Input such as text, images or audio becomes a sequence of tokens, each mapped to a vector via an embedding layer; at each layer tokens are contextualized within the context window by parallel multi-head attention, amplifying key tokens and diminishing less important ones. Positional encodings or learned positional embeddings are needed because self-attention alone is permutation-invariant. Computations parallelize across sequence positions during training more readily than recurrent networks like LSTM.

explainer.example: A sentence is split into tokens, each embedded as a vector, and multi-head attention lets the signal for key tokens be amplified while less important tokens are diminished.
